operator: Ceturb-ES / Sistema Transcol (metropolitan bus, Grande Vitória) — GVBus consortium
notes:
Built from the official Ceturb JSON API (api.onibus.ceturb.es.gov.br, OpenAPI spec at /openapi/v1.json). Endpoints used: GET /api/ConsultaLinha (395 lines returned), GET /api/BuscaItinerarios?Linha=&Tipo_Linha=T (ordered street path per direction I=ida/V=volta), GET /api/BuscaHorarios?Linha=&Tipo_Linha=T (real departure times Hora_Saida per terminal per day type). The sitrip.ceturb.es.gov.br/quadrohorario page is a Blazor Server SPA (server-rendered over SignalR) and could not be scraped client-side, but it is a front-end to the same API, which was scraped directly.

METRO/RAIL: none exists in Grande Vitória — Transcol is a metropolitan trunk-feeder bus system (route_type=3), so no rail/metro/BRT rail was applicable.

Scope: representative subset of 12 of the 395 lines — 8 intermunicipal TRUNK (troncal) lines connecting the 10 integration terminals (0500 VV/Itacibá, 0502 Laranjeiras/Itacibá, 0503 Laranjeiras/VV, 0504 Jacaraípe/Itacibá, 0507 Laranjeiras/Ibes, 0511 Carapina/Campo Grande, 0552 Campo Grande/Itaparica, 0801 Laranjeiras/Carapina) plus 4 Vitória feeder/local lines (0010, 0031, 0071, 0122). Each route has trips in both directions (0=ida, 1=volta) for 3 day types (WKD=weekday DIAS ÚTEIS, SAT=SÁBADO, SUN=DOMINGOS), 6 representative departures per direction/day-type sampled evenly across the published schedule (real clock times from the API).

Stops: modeled as the two route endpoints. For trunk lines the endpoints are the named integration terminals, geocoded to OSM/Overpass WGS-84 coordinates (amenity=bus_station in BR-ES: Carapina, Laranjeiras, Itacibá, Jardim América, São Torquato, Campo Grande, Vila Velha, Itaparica, Ibes, Jacaraípe). For feeders the endpoints are Vitória neighbourhoods/rodoviária, geocoded to known WGS-84 coordinates.

Confidence 0.62 rationale — high fidelity: route IDs/names, terminal identities and ordering, departure times, service days, and terminal coordinates are all from authoritative sources (Ceturb API + OSM WGS-84). Lower fidelity / documented approximations: (1) intermediate stops are NOT represented — the API itinerary exposes only ordered street names (Desc_Via) with no per-stop coordinates, so each route is collapsed to a terminal-to-terminal pair (no invented stops); (2) the second-endpoint arrival time is estimated by adding a fixed run time (45 min trunk / 30 min feeder) to the real departure, since the API gives only origin-terminal departures, not full timetables; (3) feeder lines expose departures from a single terminal head, so the return direction mirrors the outbound schedule; (4) only 12 of 395 lines and 3 of 5 day types (holiday/atypical omitted) are included. The full 395-line feed with all intermediate street-segment stops would require geocoding ~6006 OSM highway=bus_stop nodes against the itinerary street sequences.
